title: pay.crypto.com/graphql limit & control assessment - negative result
summary: No reportable findings. All probed DoS/limit controls are active and enforce correctly. Every verdict is derived from the raw response body of the target - no conclusion comes from a status code, a timeout, or a template. Nothing was submitted because there is nothing to report; the assessment itself is the deliverable.
key_facts: 15 requests total, sequential, sleep 1-2s; concurrency, sustained load, rate-limit probing and token enumeration excluded on purpose (volumetric DoS is out of scope for bounty programs).
Complexity budget enforced at exactly 250 (500 aliased fields rejected); query size rejected at ~10 KB; cyclic fragments rejected pre-execution.

Batching NOT SUPPORTED at any size - the endpoint does not accept operation arrays, so batch amplification is impossible regardless of per-operation limits (stricter than the 'batching enabled' claim tested against).
Introspection blocked in all 3 variants; field dedup spec-compliant; error hygiene clean (no stack traces, no internal paths).
Verdicts byte-identical across the 2026-09-26 run and the 2026-09-28 v5 re-run; draft-report replica 4/4 standard_validation with the auth-gate confirmed.

timeline.event: Negative assessment executed: 8 controls verified active, zero findings (FINAL_NEGATIVE_RESULT.md)

evidence.note: authoritative negative assessment with verbatim server responses

lessons: A negative result is a result: record it with the same rigor as a finding, or the same ground gets re-ploughed later.
Never classify from a status code or a timeout - every verdict came from the raw response body.
Re-run the suite before writing anything down: byte-identical verdicts are what make the conclusion durable.
references: crypto.com bug bounty program rules (volumetric DoS out of scope)
